literatureAccess.tools: Europe PMC REST API (search, core records with abstracts, fullTextXML) through a Node script; NCBI E-utilities efetch tried once for RFC02 and returned front matter only. WebSearch/WebFetch were not used.
literatureAccess.notAvailable: The body of Hellard 2006 (RFC02): only its abstract was retrievable. Banister 1975/1991 originals and Busso 2003 were not searched for directly. No direct study of running-performance gains in novices was found (negative searches logged).
literatureAccess.settledFromV1RC: V1RC SRC04, SRC05, SRC06, SRC08, SRC10-SRC16 are cited as settled by the predecessor record and were not re-read.
literatureAccess.rule: No effect estimate, participant count or endpoint is stated beyond what the accessed text reports. Abstract-only sources are never the sole basis of a value; where values lean on them the confidence is LOW and the value is labelled a placeholder.

counterevidence: Sought: (1) evidence that individual training-response models predict race performance well enough for an individual forecast: none found in recreational runners; elite modelling shows wide parameter uncertainty and poor generalisation (RFC02, RFC03, RFC04). (2) Evidence that recreational gains are larger than the ceilings: individualised programmes reached -6.2% in 12 weeks (RFC05) and a sub-40 group about -5% in 10 weeks (RFC06), above the INTERMEDIATE fast-edge gain alone; the fast edge also carries the V1RC margin, and the conservative choice is retained because an over-fast forecast is the harmful error (RFC01) and uncontrolled pre-post changes overstate response (RFC09). (3) Evidence against a no-taper rule: a taper benefit is real (RFC12-RFC15); omitted for the reasons in F5. (4) Evidence that no improvement should be forecast at all: low responders are common (RFC05) and disruptions frequent (RFC16), which is why the slow edge is the current estimate. Negative searches are logged in searches, not taken as proof of absence.

rulings.disposition: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS (5K, 10K, half marathon; NOVICE, INTERMEDIATE, EXPERIENCED); MODIFY (marathon: no training gain, the forecast is the current estimate); REFUSE (experience NONE, WALK_JOG/RESTART/RETURN)
rulings.ruling: A bounded, conditional forecast is admissible in V1 only as an explicitly reversible, limited scenario, not as a prediction model. It is admissible because its slow edge is the current estimate itself (no further improvement), so the forecast never asserts that a gain will happen; its fast edge is a fixed, experience-bounded ceiling scaled by observed adherence; and it is withheld whenever it is too wide, the race is far away, the evidence slows, or V1RC withholds. The predecessor abstention stands for what it said: no individually validated improvement model exists, and this record does not create one.

values.marathon: forecast = V1RC current estimate unchanged (trainingGain false)

rulings.evidenceStatus: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (magnitude and time course of an individual gain); SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (recreational runners in structured 8-15-week training improve a few percent on average with wide individual variation, including low responders)
rulings.basis: Literature for the direction and order of magnitude; sporting judgement for the envelope form; every number is a placeholder for empirical calibration
rulings.rationale: Individual impulse-response models are poorly identifiable even with dense elite data (RFC02, RFC03, RFC04); race-time conversion error is large and the fast error is the harmful one (RFC01). Group improvement in recreational runners is real but heterogeneous (RFC05: -2.9% +/- 2.4% in 12 weeks with a predefined programme; RFC06, RFC07; RFC08), and uncontrolled pre-post changes overstate true individual differences (RFC09). This supports a range anchored on measured current capacity whose slow side claims nothing, not a point prediction. Marathon: see F6.
conditions: Never a single time; range first; central never alone
Never a pace source, never an input to bands, P3, eligibility, dose, progression or the goal comparison
Experience NONE and the walk/jog, restart and return modes: no forecast
AI review is not empirical validation: every value here is to be recalibrated against estimate-versus-actual race results before any claim of accuracy

rulings.disposition: APPROVE (G_x values, unknown = EXPERIENCED, NONE = no forecast, tau, no half modifier); MODIFY (marathon gain 0)
rulings.ruling: G_x NOVICE 0.08, INTERMEDIATE 0.05, EXPERIENCED 0.03 (log of time, 10K-equivalent, R = 1, full adherence, infinite block); unknown experience uses EXPERIENCED; NONE no forecast; tau 10 weeks; half marathon: no modifier; marathon: no training gain at all (see F6).
rulings.basis: Sporting judgement, consistent in magnitude with (and for the central, below) recreational trial means; placeholders for empirical calibration
rulings.rationale: With tau 10 weeks, 12 counted weeks at full adherence give Gamma = G_x x 0.699: INTERMEDIATE 3.5% at R = 1, 1.7% at the central R 0.5. The closest trial analogue (RFC05, predefined programme, 12 weeks) reports -2.9% +/- 2.4%, other recreational trials 3-5% over 8-10 weeks (RFC06, RFC07). The central therefore sits below trial means, which is the right side: trial changes include test learning, supervision and regression to the mean (RFC09), and an over-fast forecast is the harmful error (RFC01). The fast edge also carries the V1RC margin, so it reaches a high responder of about 5-7%. NOVICE larger (larger, faster, less predictable gains in less trained people, RFC11), EXPERIENCED smaller (closer to their ceiling); an unknown class takes the smallest gain. tau 10 weeks makes gains near-linear over a typical block and saturating beyond it, consistent with a plateau under unchanged stimulus (RFC11) and with dose dependence (RFC10); its exact value is not supported by any study. No half modifier: the 10K-equivalent log gain applied to the half keeps the V1RC exponent range unchanged, and the half endurance gate stays in force.
conditions: The experience class is the one in force when the plan was created and never changes the gains already credited
The class is self-declared at intake: its use here is a coarse prior, not an assessment

rulings.disposition: APPROVE (R_c0 0.5, s0 0.3, minPairDays 28, deltaGammaMin 0.005); MODIFY (the slow edge never uses R; one endpoint pair, same kind; pair eligibility; clipping; slowdown rule)
rulings.ruling: Prior R central 0.5, sd 0.3. Update from one pair only: A = the earliest eligible reference dated no more than 28 days before the plan start or later, B = the current V1RC standard reference; same kind (RACE with RACE, field test or time trial with field test or time trial); B - A >= 28 days; Gamma(B) - Gamma(A) >= 0.005; neither presumed, lower bound (RPE <= 7), unknown effort, outside the population, nor marathon class; no declared break of 7 days or more between them. R_c clipped to [0, 1]; fast edge R_hi = min(1, R_c + 1.2816 sd); the slow edge uses R = 0 always. If B is 3% or more slower than the previous eligible same-kind reference (10K-equivalent central), g = 0 (no gain assumed) until a later reference is not slower.
rulings.basis: Sporting judgement (prior and pair rules); the noise model reuses the V1RC margins, which rest on V1RC SRC05
rulings.rationale: The proposal has an internal inconsistency: with R_c0 0.5 and s0 0.3, R_lo = 0.5 - 1.2816 x 0.3 = 0.116, not 0, so the slow edge would assume some improvement although the text says it assumes none. The slow edge is set to the current estimate in every case: training disruptions are common (RFC16), low responders are about one in five (RFC05) and recreational race-to-race variation is 2.6-4.2% (V1RC SRC05), so "no further gain" must stay inside the range. A prior centred at 0.5 with sd 0.3 (90% band 0.12-0.88) states that most athletes realise part of the ceiling and that the spread is wide (RFC08). Pair noise from the V1RC margins is the right order (pair sd 2.8-8%), so one pair moves R only a little, as it should (RFC09). Sequential updating over consecutive pairs reuses the shared reference twice and overstates precision; a single endpoint pair avoids it. Mixed race/test pairs are excluded because a race and a non-race test differ systematically in context and motivation (no quantified source: judgement). A slowdown of 3% or more (the V1RC conflict threshold, about the upper race-to-race CV) is treated as a signal, not noise: no further gain is assumed; the slower level is already in the current estimate.
conditions: No inference of illness, overtraining or any clinical state from a slower result; the existing symptom routes are unchanged

rulings.ruling: a_min 0.5, a_full 0.9; a session counts its planned minutes when reported completed, else min(actual, planned); a missing report counts 0; a week with no planned run minutes is not counted and not in the mean; pre-plan weeks earn 0; future adherence = mean a of the last <= 4 completed counted weeks, then f applied once; with none, a = 1 flagged ASSUMES_PLAN_FOLLOWED (wording: "if you follow the plan").
rulings.evidenceStatus: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (adaptation depends on dose and non-response falls with dose); PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (the 0.5 / 0.9 ramp)
rulings.basis: Literature for dose dependence; sporting judgement for the ramp; placeholders
rulings.rationale: Fitness response rises with weekly dose and non-response falls with it (RFC10). Below half of the planned running the plan is not being executed and the engine does not progress on missing data, so no gain is credited; reduced training mostly maintains (V1RC SRC16). At 90% or more the plan is effectively done. Missing reports earn nothing, as DR-149 reads absence: it is not intolerance, but it cannot justify a progression, nor a forecast gain.
conditions: Counted phases: ESTABLISHMENT, BUILD, CONSOLIDATION, DEVELOPMENT, SPECIFIC; zero credit: TAPER, RACE_WEEK, POST_EVENT, NEXT_BLOCK, hold weeks, WALK_JOG/RESTART/RETURN weeks, weeks before the plan
A week is credited to Gamma(d) only when its last day is on or before d
Run sessions only; strength sessions never count

rulings.ruling: No taper benefit is added; TAPER and RACE_WEEK earn nothing.
rulings.evidenceStatus: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (a taper benefit exists in trained athletes); INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (a quantified individual taper bonus for recreational runners)
rulings.rationale: Tapering improves performance in trained athletes (about 3%, range 0.5-6%, RFC12; ES 0.45-0.59, RFC13, RFC14), largest after pre-taper overload, which a conservative V1 plan does not prescribe. In recreational marathoners the association is 2.6% for a strict 3-week taper against a minimal one (RFC15), observational and marathon only. V1 tapers are 1 week (2 for the marathon). The current estimate usually rests on a race, already run rested, so a taper bonus would double-count. Leaving it out biases the forecast slightly slow, the safe direction.

rulings.ruling: Plan event only, on its date; shown when the race date is at most 112 days (16 weeks) after the start of the current week, and only until the day before RACE_WEEK starts; from RACE_WEEK on only the V1RC current estimate with its race-day text and pacing caution is shown (this replaces "at horizon 0 the forecast equals the current estimate", which the proposed formula does not produce: unobserved gains of past weeks would still be added). Marathon: no training gain (forecast = current estimate unchanged), every V1RC marathon gate, the block assumption, the caution, R-11 (central <= 6:00:00) and the completion-race withdrawal; the proposed fast-edge cap is moot. 5K, 10K, half: no gate beyond the V1RC endurance gates and the width test; while any V1RC Q8 down factor is in force, g = 0.
rulings.evidenceStatus: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (marathon refusal; horizon bounded by studied durations); PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (exact horizon)
rulings.basis: Literature for the marathon refusal and the horizon bound; sporting judgement for 16 weeks
rulings.rationale: Marathon: the conversion is where prediction fails and errs fast (RFC01; V1RC SRC04, SRC06); the V1RC marathon estimate already assumes the block's long runs are completed, so adding the block's gain counts the block twice; the outcome depends on pacing and fuelling more than a fitness gain captures (V1RC SRC06), and late disruptions cost 5-8% (RFC16). Horizon: the performance evidence for training gains comes from 8-15-week programmes (RFC05, RFC06, RFC07); beyond 16 weeks the curve is extrapolation. Race week: a forecast faster than the current estimate must not become a race-day pacing reference, because starting too fast is the costly error (RFC01).

rulings.disposition: APPROVE (defaults) with a permitted band for the Founder
rulings.ruling: Default W_max: 5K 0.12, 10K 0.12, half 0.15, marathon 0.18, measured on the rounded displayed values as high/low - 1. The Founder may set each anywhere up to 5K 0.18, 10K 0.18, half 0.20, marathon 0.20 without a new sporting review. The range is never narrowed to pass: it is shown whole or withheld (TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW, the current estimate still shown by V1RC).
rulings.basis: Sporting judgement against race-to-race variability; usefulness is a product choice
rulings.rationale: Recreational race-to-race variation of about 3-4% (more in slower runners, V1RC SRC05) gives a single race-day spread of roughly 10-14%; ranges narrower than that would be false precision, and ranges wider than about 20% say little beyond "about your current level". Consequence the Founder should know: at the defaults, a 10K forecast from a 5K reference (the current estimate alone is about 11.9% wide) and most novice forecasts are TOO_UNCERTAIN (examples c and h); forecasts mostly appear from same-distance race references.

rulings.ruling: All proposed withdrawals stand (hold, break >= 14 days, WALK_JOG/RESTART/RETURN, warning-sign screen required, completion race, after the race date, event estimate unavailable). Added: from RACE_WEEK on; outside the 112-day horizon; experience NONE; the V1RC extension or ESTIMATE boundary disabled; any V1RC Q8 down factor in force (g = 0, forecast = current estimate); latest result 3% or more slower (g = 0); marathon central above 6:00:00. Withdrawal applies at once; everything else changes only at the week boundary. Pace Insights withdraw on the same conditions except the slowdown and Q8 rules (they still explain).
rulings.basis: Inherited V1RC rulings plus sporting judgement
rulings.rationale: Each added condition only withholds a claim or removes a gain; none prescribes anything.
conditions: The goal is compared with the current estimate only (V1RC Q7.goal), never with the forecast

rulings.ruling: Comparability, the 42-day window, 3 executions, 14-day span, 2/3 majority with the latest included, STABLE/MIXED/INSUFFICIENT_DATA and the week-boundary computation are approved. FASTER/INSIDE/SLOWER use the same comparison as V1RC Q8 (band in force in the execution's own week, trigger 1.5%). EXCEPTIONAL: |d - median(d)| > max(3 MAD, 0.05), with d = ln(band midpoint pace / execution pace), each against the band of its own week. A confirmed insight never changes capacity, an estimate or the forecast in V1: only a qualifying race or test does. Actions as proposed (explain Q8 where it has room; otherwise offer the V1RC field test when P3 offers one, else suggest reporting a race; accepting runs the existing P3 flow).
rulings.basis: V1RC rulings and literature for no capacity change; sporting judgement for thresholds
rulings.rationale: Training pace at a reported effort is not race capacity: it varies with conditions, fatigue and GPS error (3.2-6.1% mean distance error, V1RC SRC13), and V1RC already rules that upward training evidence moves bands only, never estimates. A 3% floor would discard ordinary in-band sessions as exceptional (example PI-1); 5% sits above typical GPS error.
conditions: Suggestions are offers under every P3 rule (no test in TAPER/RACE_WEEK/POST_EVENT, not within 14 days of the race, at most 1 per 42 days, novices 3 km only, not while the screen is required, RC-01 respected); never a prompt to race
Short reps (< 5 min bouts) and easy runs faster at RPE <= 4: informative only, never a suggestion; the easy ceiling never moves faster from them and no copy invites faster easy running
SLOWER_THAN_BAND: "effort governs, slow to the cue"

Harder-than-cue executions (excluded from the vote by the RPE rule) may be stated as a fact: "these sessions felt harder than intended"; the copy may name only the V1RC factors (heat, hills, wind, fatigue) and say the plan's weekly review already reads harder-than-intended sessions. It never mentions illness, overtraining, readiness or anything clinical, never suggests a deload or rest of its own, and points to symptoms only through the existing warning-sign entry, never by inference

rulings.ruling: No heart-rate input to the forecast or the insights in V1; V1RC zones stay display-only.
rulings.rationale: HR-speed indices were used in RFC05 only under research conditions (chest strap, standardized protocols); in the app HR drifts with heat, hydration and fatigue, wrist sensors are less accurate, and no index is validated for forecasting.

rulings.disposition: OPINION: ACCEPTABLE_WITH_CONDITIONS (the formal reading of the catalog rule is Founder/PCG)
rulings.ruling: Sporting opinion: compatible with "claim ... finish time or fitness gain" only because the slow edge assumes no further improvement, so no gain is claimed, and only with these changes. Before any completed week: "Forecast for <race> on <date>, if you follow the plan: <low>-<high>. The slower end assumes no further improvement. Not a promise." After: "... if you keep training as you have over the last <n> weeks: ...". Always state the reference and its date and "individual results vary". Never "you will run", "predicted time", "on track", "achievable", never a single time, never next to the goal as a verdict. Marathon: "Your current marathon estimate, assuming the block's long runs are completed: <low>-<high>. No further improvement is assumed for the marathon. Not a promise."
rulings.rationale: A conditional range that contains "no gain" does not assert a gain or a time; the risk is the reader taking the fast edge as the expectation, which the wording and the race-week cut contain. This opinion does not interpret the product rule; that reading belongs to the Founder and PCG and is still required before athlete-facing use (V1RC recheck).

rulings.ruling: Ten forecast examples (a-h with d2, e1, e2) plus horizon, race-week and one Pace Insights example, in workedExamples.
rulings.rationale: Computed from values.forecast by a scratch script; the implementation must reproduce them to the second.

values.scope: Additive over COACHINGCORE-V1-RUN-CALIBRATION-FREEZE-1. No V1RC value, gate or behaviour changes. Nonclinical recreational adults, synthetic data only.

forecast.start: The V1RC current estimate of the plan's event, its unrounded {lower, central, upper} as V1RC computes them (after any Q8 down adjustment). No forecast when that estimate is UNAVAILABLE or not shown.
forecast.weekCreditedWhen: Its last day is on or before the date at which Gamma is evaluated

adherence.sessionMinutes: Run sessions only: planned minutes if reported completed, else min(actual minutes, planned minutes); a missing report counts 0
adherence.weekWithoutPlannedRunMinutes: Not counted (0 credit) and left out of the mean
adherence.futureMeanOf: a (the weekly adherence), then f applied once

response.pair: One pair: A = the earliest eligible reference dated on or after (plan start - 28 days); B = the current V1RC standard reference. Same kind (RACE_RESULT with RACE_RESULT; TIME_TRIAL or FIELD_TEST with TIME_TRIAL or FIELD_TEST). Neither presumed, SUBMAXIMAL_LOWER_BOUND, unknown effort, OUTSIDE_MODEL_POPULATION, nor longer than the half marathon. No declared break of 7 days or more between A and B.
response.sigma: The V1RC margin of each reference (tier margin plus any slow-runner margin) / 1.2816
response.update: R_obs = ln(T10_A / T10_B) / dGamma; var = (sigma_A^2 + sigma_B^2) / dGamma^2; R_c = (R_c0/s0^2 + R_obs/var) / (1/s0^2 + 1/var); sd = (1/s0^2 + 1/var)^(-1/2); then R_c clipped to [0, 1]. No pair: R_c = 0.5, sd = 0.3.

slowdown.comparedWith: the most recent eligible same-kind reference dated before B (pair rules except spacing)
slowdown.effect: g = 0 until a later reference is not 3% slower

formulas.H_eff: sum of f(a_w) over credited counted plan weeks; future counted weeks before RACE_WEEK each earn f(a_future)
formulas.g: Gamma(start of RACE_WEEK) - Gamma(date of the current reference); 0 for the marathon, after a slowdown, or while a Q8 down factor is in force

forecast.rounding: V1RC roundOutwardSeconds (5K/10K 15 s, half/marathon 60 s): low floored, high ceiled, central to nearest
forecast.width: rounded high / rounded low - 1; shown only if <= wMax, else TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW; never narrowed
forecast.shownUntil: The day before RACE_WEEK starts; from RACE_WEEK only the V1RC current estimate, race-day text and pacing caution

confidence.withoutGain: the current estimate tier, at most MODERATE

forecast.recompute: At the week boundary only; withdrawal applies at once
forecast.goalComparison: With the V1RC current estimate only, never with the forecast
withdrawal: declared break of 14 days or more
event estimate unavailable or not shown
extension or ESTIMATE boundary not enabled

requiredText.beforeAnyWeek: Forecast for <race> on <date>, if you follow the plan: <low>-<high>. The slower end assumes no further improvement. Not a promise.
requiredText.afterWeeks: Forecast for <race> on <date>, if you keep training as you have over the last <n> weeks: <low>-<high>. The slower end assumes no further improvement. Not a promise.
requiredText.basis: Based on your <reference> of <date>; individual results vary.
requiredText.marathon: Your current marathon estimate, assuming the block's long runs are completed: <low>-<high>. No further improvement is assumed for the marathon. Not a promise.

paceInsights.comparable: V1RC comparableRun (no HEAT, HILLY, TRAIL, WIND_STRONG; no treadmill; GPS not poor), completed, RPE inside the cue, every work bout >= 5 min
paceInsights.classify: As V1RC Q8 against the band in force in the execution's own week: FASTER if fast edge pace / pace - 1 > 0.015; SLOWER if pace / slow edge pace - 1 > 0.015; else INSIDE

exceptional.measure: d = ln(band midpoint pace / execution pace), band of its own week
exceptional.rule: |d - median(d)| > max(3 * MAD(d), 0.05): shown, never voted

outcomes.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: fewer than 3 non-exceptional or span < 14 days

actions.q8NoRoomOr5K10K: OFFER_V1RC_FIELD_TEST if P3 offers one now, else SUGGEST_REPORTING_A_RACE

Computed at the start of week 7; future counted weeks 7-14 = 8.

forecast.title: (d2) As (d) with B 4% slower: no gain assumed
forecast.inputs: As (d) but B = 10K race 52:00 (4.0% slower than A, at or above the 3% threshold): g = 0, the forecast equals the current estimate, flag NO_GAIN_LATEST_RESULT_SLOWER.

output.confidence: current estimate tier, at most MODERATE

forecast.title: (e1) Marathon that passes
forecast.inputs: Marathon block, 16 weeks, starts 2027-01-04, race 2027-04-25, every V1RC/V1FC marathon eligibility criterion met, race day not a completion. Reference: half marathon 1:50:00 OFFICIAL 2026-12-20 (CURRENT at week 5), HIGH. Experience INTERMEDIATE. The marathon earns no training gain: the forecast is the V1RC current marathon estimate unchanged, with its caution and assumption; central 4:01:00 <= 6:00:00 (R-11 met); width 15.0% <= 0.18.

output.confidence: current estimate tier, at most MODERATE

forecast.title: (e2) Marathon that fails
forecast.inputs: As (e1) but the half is 2:45:00 (10K-equivalent 74.2 min, inside the V1RC population). Marathon central 6:01:00 > 6:00:00: withheld under recheck ruling (c)/R-11; neither forecast nor current marathon estimate is shown.

output.confidence: current estimate tier, at most MODERATE

forecast.title: (f) Plan start, no completed week: ASSUMES_PLAN_FOLLOWED
forecast.inputs: Plan for a 5K, 10 weeks, starts 2027-01-04; weeks 1-8 counted, 9 TAPER, 10 RACE_WEEK; race 2027-03-14. Reference 5K race 25:00 OFFICIAL 2026-12-25, HIGH. INTERMEDIATE. Computed at the start of week 1: no completed week, future adherence assumed 1 and flagged; the wording says "if you follow the plan".

forecast.title: (g) Experienced (or unknown experience), GPS-measured 10K, MODERATE
forecast.inputs: As (a) but experience EXPERIENCED (an unknown class uses the same value), reference 10K race 45:00 measured by GPS (one tier down: MODERATE, m = 0.04), adherence 1.0 in weeks 1-4.

forecast.title: (h) 10K forecast from a 5K reference: too uncertain at the default width
forecast.inputs: As (a) but the reference is a 5K race 22:00 OFFICIAL, HIGH, longest run 55 min. The current 10K estimate alone is 11.9% wide; with the gain the forecast is 15.9% wide > 0.12: TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW (the current estimate is still shown by V1RC). It would show only if the Founder chose a 10K width of 0.16 or more inside the permitted band (<= 0.18).

horizon.title: (i) Race beyond the horizon
horizon.inputs: 10K race Sun 2027-06-27, 26-week plan starting 2027-01-04, computed at the start of week 1.

raceWeek.title: (j) Race week
raceWeek.inputs: Example (a) at the start of week 16 (RACE_WEEK).

output.shown: the V1RC current estimate 48:45-51:15 with its race-day text and pacing caution only

paceInsights.result: IMPROVING (3 of 4 non-exceptional executions FASTER = 0.75 >= 2/3, the latest FASTER, span 21 days >= 14)
paceInsights.action: EXPLAIN_ONLY: the existing weekly rule (V1RC Q8) adjusts the threshold band; no test is suggested because Q8 has room in this domain; capacity, estimates and the forecast are unchanged
paceInsights.note: Under the proposed 3% floor the 2027-02-08 execution (an ordinary in-band session, 4.5% from the median) would be EXCEPTIONAL and dropped from the vote; under the ruled 5% floor it votes. GPS distance error of 3.2-6.1% (V1RC SRC13) is why the floor is 5%.

conditions: C1: Additive only: no V1RC value, gate, band, estimate or behaviour changes; the forecast reads V1RC outputs and never writes to them.
C2: The forecast never feeds pace bands, tests, estimates, goal comparison, dose, progression, phase, eligibility or race-day mode.
C3: The slow edge is always the current estimate high edge; the forecast is a range, central never alone, never a single time.
C4: Before any athlete-facing use, the Founder/PCG reading of the catalog rule "finish time or fitness gain" is recorded (V1RC escalation still open).
C5: Every value is a placeholder until calibrated against estimate-versus-actual race results; the first such data is a re-review trigger. No accuracy claim in copy.
C6: Wording per values.forecast.requiredText (Product owns final copy; meaning may not drift).
C7: No clinical inference from any slowdown, harder-than-cue session or missing data; existing symptom routes only.
C8: A fresh SSCTR instance judges the implementation against these worked examples; the implementation reproduces every forecastSeconds, status and flag exactly.
C9: Synthetic data only in this mission; V1 authority NO.

aeReview.level: Offline sporting decision on a display-only forecast and an explanation-only insight; no plan mutation.
aeReview.q1_currentPlanAdequate: Not assessed by the forecast; the forecast never judges or changes the plan.
aeReview.q2_materialFact: Facts are V1RC references, logged sessions and the plan calendar, with provenance.
aeReview.q3_keepDefensible: Yes: the plan is unchanged by design.
aeReview.q4_changeNecessary: No plan change; Pace Insights may offer the existing P3 test, which the athlete accepts or not.
aeReview.q5_smallestIntervention: Explain only, or an offer under existing P3 rules.
aeReview.q6_smallerAlternativesInsufficient: Not applicable: no intervention is made.
aeReview.q9_uncertainty: Individual gain magnitude and time course are uncertain; ranges, withholding and the no-gain slow edge carry it.
aeReview.q10_askHoldClinical: No ASK or HOLD added; clinical routes unchanged.

changedFromProposal: Slow edge always = current estimate (the proposal's R_lo was 0.116 with no data, contradicting its own text)
Marathon: no training gain; forecast = current estimate
Horizon 26 -> 16 weeks (112 days); not shown from RACE_WEEK (replaces "horizon 0 = current estimate")
One endpoint pair of the same kind instead of sequential consecutive pairs; pair eligibility rules; reference A no earlier than 28 days before the plan
Slowdown rule: latest reference >= 3% slower -> g = 0
Q8 down factor in force -> g = 0
W_max: defaults kept, a permitted band up to 0.18/0.18/0.20/0.20 for the Founder
Goal compared with the current estimate only, not the forecast

escalations.what: Formal reading of catalog productMustNot "Claim injury prevention, readiness, finish time or fitness gain" for a conditional forecast whose fast edge includes possible gain. Sporting opinion in F11. Blocks athlete-facing use, not these values.

Copy for every required text; semantics of the self-declared experience class, the "completed" flag, missing reports and reference kinds (RACE_RESULT vs TIME_TRIAL/FIELD_TEST).

literature.citation: Vickers AJ, Vertosick EA. An empirical study of race times in recreational endurance runners. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil 2016;8:26.
literature.locator: Re-opened in this run: Abstract; Methods passage on k = 1.07 and the penalized error. Settled detail as V1RC SRC01.
literature.findingsUsed: Riegel well calibrated to the half marathon, at least 10 min too fast in the marathon for half of runners (settled in V1RC). New passage used here: the authors penalize over-estimation of velocity because "a runner who starts too fast will slow dramatically", whereas one who starts too slow can speed up: the error that matters is the fast one.
limitations: cross-sectional: predicts across distances, not across time

literature.citation: Hellard P, Avalos M, Lacoste L, Barale F, Chatard JC, Millet GP. Assessing the limitations of the Banister model in monitoring training. J Sports Sci 2006;24(5):509-20.
literature.locator: Abstract (Europe PMC and NCBI efetch returned the front matter only; the body was not retrievable)
literature.findingsUsed: Nine elite swimmers over a season: the impulse-response model fitted (R2 0.79) but 95% CIs of the useful time constants were wide (e.g. fitness 38 [17-59] d, fatigue 19 [6-32] d) and parameters were highly correlated, making interpretation "worthless".
limitations: elite swimmers, dense data: a recreational runner with 1-3 references per block is far less identifiable

literature.citation: Imbach F, Perrey S, Chailan R, Meline T, Candau R. Training load responses modelling and model generalisation in elite sports. Sci Rep 2022;12:1586.
literature.findingsUsed: Seven elite skaters over three months: the variable dose-response model generalised worse than regularised statistical models under time-series cross-validation; the authors make a generalisation procedure a prerequisite for any predictive model.

literature.citation: Wang W, Zhao Y, Hou X, et al. Advancing training effectiveness prediction in mass sport through longitudinal data: a mathematical model approach based on the Fitness-Fatigue Model. PLoS One 2025;20(12):e0337824.
literature.findingsUsed: Individually fitted fitness-fatigue models with dense daily data in 13 cyclists: predictive MAPE 4-32%, up to 87% for some individuals.

literature.citation: Nuuttila OP, Nummela A, Korhonen E, Hakkinen K, Kyrolainen H. Individualized endurance training based on recovery and training status in recreational runners. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2022;54(10):1690-1701.
literature.locator: Abstract; Methods (participants, protocol); Table 1; Results summary; Limitations
literature.findingsUsed: Recreational runners running at least 4 times a week (VO2max about 46 mL/kg/min, age 34-37): over 12 weeks (6-wk volume + 6-wk interval periods) 10-km time changed -2.9% +/- 2.4% with a predefined programme and -6.2% +/- 2.8% with individualised adjustment; 21-23% low responders in the predefined group.
limitations: no non-training control: changes include test learning and within-subject noise

literature.citation: Munoz I, Seiler S, Bautista J, Espana J, Larumbe E, Esteve-Lanao J. Does polarized training improve performance in recreational runners? Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2014;9(2):265-72.
literature.locator: Abstract (results sentence truncated in the record)
literature.findingsUsed: 30 recreational runners, 10 weeks, 10-km race before and after: both groups improved; the polarized group from 39:18 to 37:19 (about -5%). Same paper as V1RC SRC24.
limitations: abstract only, second group values not visible

literature.citation: Festa L, Tarperi C, Skroce K, La Torre A, Schena F. Effects of different training intensity distribution in recreational runners. Front Sports Act Living 2019;1:70.
literature.findingsUsed: 38 recreational runners, 8 weeks: 2-km average velocity +3.5% and +3.0% in the two TRIMP-matched programmes.

literature.citation: Mann TN, Lamberts RP, Lambert MI. High responders and low responders: factors associated with individual variation in response to standardized training. Sports Med 2014;44(8):1113-24.
literature.findingsUsed: A wide range of individual responses to standardized endurance training is common; pre-training phenotype predicts little of the response; stimulus, recovery, lifestyle and measurement error all contribute.

literature.citation: Atkinson G, Batterham AM. True and false interindividual differences in the physiological response to an intervention. Exp Physiol 2015;100(6):577-88.
literature.findingsUsed: Within-subject random variation and regression to the mean can explain apparent individual response differences; true variation needs a comparator SD.

literature.citation: Montero D, Lundby C. Refuting the myth of non-response to exercise training: "non-responders" do respond to higher dose of training. J Physiol 2017;595(11):3377-87.
literature.findingsUsed: 78 healthy adults, 1-5 x 60 min/week for 6 weeks: non-response of fitness declined with weekly dose and was abolished by 2 more sessions a week.

literature.citation: Scharhag-Rosenberger F, Meyer T, Walitzek S, Kindermann W. Time course of changes in endurance capacity: a 1-yr training study. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2009;41(5):1130-7.
literature.findingsUsed: 18 previously untrained adults, 3 x 45 min/week jogging at a constant 60% HR reserve for 12 months: VO2max +16% median; no further significant change after 6 months at an unchanged stimulus.

literature.citation: Mujika I, Padilla S. Scientific bases for precompetition tapering strategies. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2003;35(7):1182-7.
literature.findingsUsed: Tapering usually improves performance by about 3% (usual range 0.5-6%), keeping intensity and cutting volume.

literature.citation: Bosquet L, Montpetit J, Arvisais D, Mujika I. Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007;39(8):1358-65.
literature.findingsUsed: 27 studies of competitive athletes: a 2-week taper with volume cut 41-60% gave the largest effect (ES 0.59 +/- 0.33).

literature.citation: Wang Z, Wang YT, Gao W, Zhong Y. Effects of tapering on performance in endurance athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS One 2023;18(5):e0282838.
literature.locator: Abstract; Methods (analysis); Results passages on volume reduction
literature.findingsUsed: 14 studies: time-trial SMD -0.45 after tapering; no change in VO2max or economy; tapering after pre-taper overload had the larger effect.

literature.citation: Smyth B, Lawlor A. Longer disciplined tapers improve marathon performance for recreational runners. Front Sports Act Living 2021;3:735220.
literature.locator: Abstract; Methods (taper definition, finish-time benefit vs a relaxed 1-week taper); Limitations; Conclusions
literature.findingsUsed: More than 158,000 recreational marathoners: strict 3-week tapers were associated with a median finish-time saving of 5 min 32 s (2.6%) relative to a minimal (relaxed 1-week) taper.
limitations: ability proxied by fastest training 10 km
baseline is a minimal taper, not no taper

literature.citation: Feely C, Smyth B, Caulfield B, Lawlor A. Estimating the cost of training disruptions on marathon performance. Front Sports Act Living 2022;4:1096124.
literature.findingsUsed: 300,000 recreational marathoners: over half had short disruptions (<= 6 days); disruptions of 7 days or more were associated with a 5-8% slower finish (within-runner comparison), more when late in training.

literature.citation: Bacon AP, Carter RE, Ogle EA, Joyner MJ. VO2max trainability and high intensity interval training in humans: a meta-analysis. PLoS One 2013;8(9):e73182.
literature.findingsUsed: Sedentary or recreationally active adults, 6-13 weeks of interval training: VO2max +0.51 L/min on average, heterogeneity I2 = 70.
